attempts.label: DANDI:001882
attempts.paper_title: Prevalence of IMPG1 and IMPG2 Mutations Leading to Retinitis Pigmentosa or Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy in a Cohort of Patients with Inherited Retinal Dystrophies
attempts.entry_title: IMPG1 and IMPG2 variants in retinal dystrophy patients (Yuan et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The patient table, the prevalence (7 of 480) and the gnomAD frequencies held in this data, but the pathogenicity scores, the stability predictions and the novelty of IMPG1 p.Asp423Glu did not. The IMPG1 scores, CADD and FATHMM differ from Table 2, and p.Asp423Glu is already a ClinVar entry. I-Mutant gave stabilizing values for 4 of 5 variants, though that rests on a sequence-only reading the paper does not state. The patient imaging descriptions held only in part, and the deposit holds just the paper's own figure panels, so they are not independent evidence. The residue-interaction analyses, ancestry and the EOG could not be tested because the structure models and clinical data are not deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Yuan, Chatterjee, Leys, Odom and Salido (2025) on dandiset 001882, which holds a table of the seven patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 variants, a document of in silico tool outputs and the paper's four figures as image files. It checks the patients' genotypes, diagnoses and acuities, reads the phenotypes on the deposited figure panels, and retests the in silico findings (domains, pathogenicity scores, ClinVar, ProtParam values, gnomAD frequencies) with pinned outside services.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yuan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001882

outcomes.notes: The spreadsheet holds 7 IMPG carriers (5 IMPG2, 2 IMPG1), 2 with RP (F32, M83) and 5 with VMD. Over the paper's cohort of 480 these are 1.458%, 0.417% and 1.042%, within 10% of 1.45%, 0.41% and 1.04% (and equal to them truncated to two decimals); 480/7 = 68.6, the Discussion's 1 in 68. The dandiset holds no patient outside the seven, so the denominator could not be checked.
deviations: The cohort size of 480 is taken from the paper (Methods 2.1), as the criterion allows when the dataset holds only the carriers; the second measured value is that number, not a measurement.

outcomes.notes: No file and no metadata field records race, ethnicity or ancestry; the spreadsheet's headers and the dandiset description were searched for race, ethnic, Caucasian, white, European and ancestry, with no hit.

All 7 patients match Table 1 in gene, cDNA change, protein change and zygosity (7 of 7, no field differs after normalising spaces around ';' and '&'). The spreadsheet writes F32's gene as IMPG1, where Table 1 prints IMGP1.
deviations: The spreadsheet looks like the authors' source for Table 1 (same patient labels and fields, with an extra column), so the test shows that the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence of the clinical findings.

outcomes.notes: Diagnoses match for 7 of 7 patients, compared with the spreadsheet's diagnosis column. Sex and age exist only in the patient label (F32 and so on), the label the paper uses, so their match (7 of 7) is true by construction and is not an independent measurement; no date of any kind is recorded, so the readings of age (at the last visit, or in 2024) cannot be told apart.
deviations: The spreadsheet looks like the authors' source for Table 1 (same patient labels and fields, with an extra column), so the test shows that the deposit agrees with the paper, not independent evidence of the clinical findings.

Not an assumption the outcome rests on, since the outcome is partial under every reading. Neither the paper nor the claims file says what makes a lesion hyper-autofluorescent; the paper graded by inspection. Five readings of a bright focus are run on every eye (95th percentile above 1.1 or 1.0 of the surround, above 1.1 of the adjacent macula, and 95th percentile or maximum brighter than in 95% of same-size background discs of the same panel, which lie on the perimacular ring). The last is adopted, since hyper-autofluorescence is a lesion brighter than the fundus around it, and it calibrates brighter on the panel's own perimacular ring while keeping a small focus. The readings agree on every eye except M73's right (bright under the 1.0 surround and the macula readings, not under the other three) and M73's left (not bright under the background 95th percentile reading).

Under two of the other readings his right eye is bright too, and all three parts of the criterion would hold. The criterion gives no rule for a partial result; partially reproduced is used because two of its three parts hold and the third holds in one eye.

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no EOG; none of EOG, electro-oculogram or Arden occurs in any of its text (spreadsheet, Word document, folder script, metadata), and no file is an electrophysiology recording.
The dandiset holds no genetic report beyond the IMPG variants of the spreadsheet; none of JAG1, BEST1, ALMS1, CEP164, COL11A1, CPLANE1, EYS, KIF7, NPHP4 or PHYH occurs in any of its text.

No reading places all 7; UniProt, InterPro and the PROSITE profiles place 6, Pfam and SMART 4. UniProt (Q17R60 v129, Q9BZV3 v146); IMPG1 has only SEA 1 (232-354) and SEA 2 (571-684), no EGF-like domain, so p.Leu740Phe cannot be near one; the other 6 hold. InterPro 110.0 and PROSITE profiles; IMPG1 has an EGF-like domain at 684-722, 18 residues before Leu740 (near, the closest domain, not in it), but IMPG2 has a single EGF-like domain (1010-1051), so p.Arg1088* lies in no EGF-like 2 domain; the other 6 hold. Pfam 38.2 and SMART 9.0 annotate only the two SEA domains of each protein, so p.Leu740Phe, p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Arg1088* fail. p.Arg131Cys is 108 residues from SEA1 and 109 from the end of the signal peptide (1-22), so 'near SEA-1' rests on one residue if the signal peptide counts as a domain. The paper's own 'in' for p.Leu740Phe holds under no reading. The spreadsheet's 'Location of Variant' column places p.Leu740Phe 'Post EGF-like 1', after the domain.
deviations: UniProt entries are pinned through UniSave at the versions current in November 2024 (Q17R60 v129 and Q9BZV3 v146, both released 2 October 2024 and replaced on 27 November 2024, as cell 61 prints); InterPro is read from its current release (110.0), which cannot be pinned through its API.

outcomes.notes: SIFT and PolyPhen-2 HumVar (Ensembl VEP release 116, MANE Select transcripts) match Table 2 exactly for the three IMPG2 missense variants (SIFT 0, 0, 0; PolyPhen 0.996, 0.645, 0.998) but not for IMPG1; VEP gives SIFT 0.02 for p.Leu740Phe and 0.09 for p.Asp423Glu, the paper's two values exchanged, and PolyPhen 0.106 and 0.043 (paper 0.575 and 0.98). PolyPhen-2 HumDiv (dbNSFP 4.8a) gives 0.575 for p.Leu740Phe as the paper does, 3 of 5 values within tolerance, but 0.31 for p.Asp423Glu. VEP calls p.Asp423Glu tolerated (SIFT) and benign (PolyPhen), against the paper's Pathogenic, so the Prediction column is not matched. CADD PHRED matches at most 2 of 7 values under any of GRCh37 or GRCh38 and v1.6 or v1.7; the nonsense variants score 36 to 45 against 11.2 and 13.4. No FATHMM, FATHMM-MKL or FATHMM-XF coding score and no MutationTaster score in dbNSFP matches the paper's columns (0 of 5 and 0 of 7), under any value of dbNSFP's per-transcript or per-model lists; the FATHMM-MKL web server gives the same coding scores as dbNSFP (0.83 to 0.99 for the IMPG2 variants, against 0.0076 to 0.0577) and matches 0 of 5, coding or non-coding. The MutationTaster2021 API redirects to the GeneCascade home page, even for its own documented example, so the paper's 0 to 100 MutationTaster score could not be recomputed. The paper's ids for p.Leu740Phe and p.Arg964* (rs15048636, rs267606975) differ from the variants' ids (rs150486366, rs267606875); the dandiset's Word document gives rs267606875.
deviations: The web tools of November 2024 cannot be called in a pinned version. SIFT and PolyPhen-2 HumVar come from Ensembl VEP (release 116); PolyPhen-2 HumDiv, FATHMM and MutationTaster from dbNSFP 4.8a (MyVariant.info build 20250624), whose MutationTaster score is a probability, not the paper's 0 to 100 score; FATHMM-MKL also from the FATHMM web server as it answers today; CADD from its versioned API.
dbNSFP's per-transcript lists (SIFT, FATHMM) cannot always be lined up with its transcript list, since MyVariant.info drops missing entries; every list value is shown and a match by any value counts.
MutationTaster2021, which gives a 0 to 100 tree vote, was tried through its API and does not answer.
SIFT and PolyPhen-2 were not run on GRCh37 in the notebook; VEP's GRCh37 service took 12 minutes while preparing (not run here).

outcomes.notes: IMPG1 c.1269C>A on NM_001563.4 is GRCh38 6:76002940 G>T (rs758038128). It is ClinVar variation 1000102, NM_001563.4(IMPG1):c.1269C>A (p.Asp423Glu), a missense variant of uncertain significance in IMPG1, in all 4 ClinVar VCF releases of November 2024 (3, 11, 20 and 26 November). It first appears in the release of 15 March 2021 (the release of 8 March 2021 lacks it), from one submission last evaluated on 28 August 2020, with the condition 'not provided'; so ClinVar records no association with VMD, and the claim's second half (first association with VMD) is not contradicted. The same position also carries a synonymous G>A record (1156378).

Tested on the two sequence-based tools; the 15 values of mCSM, SDM and DUET need the I-TASSER models of Methods 2.3, which are not deposited. MuPRO (web server, sequence only) gives a negative DDG for all 5 variants and matches Table 3 for 3 of 5 (p.Leu740Phe -0.930, p.Asp423Glu -0.478, p.Arg131Cys -0.627); it gives p.Cys1019Tyr -0.887 (Table 3 -1.266) and p.Leu249Phe -1.2666 (Table 3 -1.525), so Table 3's p.Cys1019Tyr value is MuPRO's p.Leu249Phe value, which the Word document gives for p.Leu249Phe. I-Mutant 2.0 (web server, sequence, 25 C, pH 7) gives a positive, stabilizing DDG for 4 of 5 (p.Leu740Phe +0.19, p.Asp423Glu +0.88, p.Cys1019Tyr +0.14, p.Leu249Phe +0.55) and -1.22 for p.Arg131Cys; for IMPG2 these are Table 3's magnitudes (0.14, 0.55) with the sign reversed, and -1.22 is the Word document's value (Table 3 -1.13). Its sign classifier calls p.Asp423Glu an increase in stability (reliability 8 of 10). So under either I-Mutant output not every variant is destabilizing by every tool, and the claim's first part fails on a tool the paper names. The ranking cannot be tested on all five tools; p.Leu249Phe is the most destabilizing under MuPRO and p.Arg131Cys under I-Mutant. On Table 3's own values every entry is negative and p.Leu249Phe has the most negative mean (-1.25). The Word document holds 23 of the 25 values; 20 agree within 10%, and it gives SDM +0.58 (Stabilizing) for p.Asp423Glu where Table 3 prints -0.52. The outcome rests on the claims file's reading that iMutant is run from sequence; the paper does not name the mode, neither sequence output gives Table 3's IMPG1 values (-0.85, -0.76), and the regression and the classifier disagree in sign for p.Leu740Phe, p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Leu249Phe, so the paper may have used the structure mode on the undeposited models (asked of a reader in questions/001882.yaml).
deviations: mCSM, SDM and DUET were not run: they need the I-TASSER models, which are not deposited, and a rerun of I-TASSER (a queued web server with stochastic output) was not tried. 15 of the 25 values are therefore not computed.

MuPRO and I-Mutant 2.0 were run on their web servers as they answer today (no version can be pinned), on the UniProt sequences Q17R60 v129 and Q9BZV3 v146, the criterion's reading; I-Mutant at its default 25 C and pH 7, in both its DDG regression and sign classifier modes.

Assumption. iMutant is run from sequence, as the criterion says. The paper does not say so; Methods 2.4 gives only the server's address, its reference 46 is 'I-Mutant2.0, Predicting stability changes upon mutation from the protein sequence or structure', and Methods 2.3 built I-TASSER models 'for further analysis'. The structure mode cannot be run, since the models are not deposited, so the outcome rests on the sequence reading and on one tool, in one mode, on a server with no version. Under MuPRO alone every value is negative.

outcomes.notes: DynaMut needs the I-TASSER models of Methods 2.3, which are not deposited anywhere; a rerun of I-TASSER (a queued web server with stochastic output, the claims file's only reading) was not tried. The dandiset holds the residue-contact images of Figure 4A,B only.

As for impg1-interactions-unchanged. The dandiset holds the residue-contact images of Figure 4C-E; in that file the images of the top row show Arg131 and Cys131 and the middle row Cys1019 and Tyr1019, while the labels beside them read p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Leu249Phe (read by eye).

Reading (a), the full UniProt sequence (Q17R60 v129, 797 residues), gives 14 of 18 values; all 6 of the reference (89,387.4 Da, pI 4.793, 12,450 atoms, instability 53.57, aliphatic 75.63, GRAVY -0.482) and all 6 of p.Leu740Phe, and the instability (53.76) and aliphatic (75.63) indices of p.Asp423Glu. Its weight (89,401.4 against 89,419), pI (4.796 against 4.81), atoms (12,453 against 12,457) and GRAVY (-0.482 against -0.474) do not match; an Asp to Phe change at 423 gives Table 4's p.Asp423Glu column (89,419.5, 4.81, 12,457, 53.76, 75.63, -0.474). The directions the text states all hold. Reading (b), without the signal peptide, matches no value. The pI is computed with Biopython's Bjellqvist pK values, not ExPASy's own code; the reference matches (4.793), and Asp to Glu moves it by +0.003 where Table 4 moves it by +0.02 (Asp to Phe, +0.017), so a small difference between the codes would not bring 4.796 to 4.81.
deviations: Values are computed with ProtParam's definitions (ExPASy average residue masses, the Bjellqvist pK values and the instability index as Biopython implements ProtParam, the Ikai aliphatic index, Kyte-Doolittle GRAVY) in place of the web tool.

outcomes.notes: Under gnomAD v4.1 joint allele counts with '1 in N' read as 1/(2 x allele frequency) (one carrier in N individuals), all 6 values are within 10%; 1 in 98,335 (p.Cys1019Tyr, 6 of 1,180,016 European non-Finnish alleles), 4,096 and 3,031 (p.Arg131Cys, European non-Finnish and Middle Eastern), 18,722 and 58,997 (p.Arg964*, African/African American and European non-Finnish) and 332 (p.Leu740Phe). v4.1 exomes match 4 of 6; v4.1 genomes, v3.1.2 genomes and the 1/allele frequency reading match none. p.Cys1019Tyr is absent from v3.1.2.
deviations: The paper names no gnomAD version; the readings of the criterion were run and one combination matches all values. The gnomAD API prints no release number; that gnomad_r4 is v4.1 comes from gnomAD's documentation, not from an output of the notebook.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds no clinical recording. The fundus photographs, FAF, angiograms, OCT and Goldmann fields exist only as the annotated, cropped panels of the paper's Figures 2 and 3 (one image per modality and eye, one OCT B-scan per eye, a single angiogram frame per eye). The EOG of patient M73, the genetic panel reports (the JAG1, BEST1 and other variants the Discussion cites), race or ethnicity, visit dates and any record of the other 473 patients of the cohort are not in it.

The first column of the spreadsheet 'derivatives/small table for 7 patients 20241127.xlsx' holds what look like hospital record numbers of the seven patients, in a public CC0 dataset. The attempt did not print or use them.

The metadata give 1 subject, 4 samples and no species, approach or measurement technique, while the files describe seven human patients. The figure files are named as BIDS microscopy samples (sub-01/micr/sub-01_sample-0N_microscopy.ome.tif.tif, one .ome.tif.jpg) but are RGB figure exports from Adobe Illustrator, not OME-TIFF and not microscopy; one is named 'Fig 3. VMD 20241122.1-01.tif'.

The paper is named only in the description, not in relatedResource. No file describes the spreadsheet's columns (the 'Location of Variant' column is not in the paper; Refraction, clinVar and Pathogenicity are empty) or says which figure each image file is.
Five identical Google Drive desktop.ini files and the script setup_bids.py, which only makes the folder layout and a dataset_description.json that is not deposited, are among the 13 assets.

The Word document 'sourcedata/protein structure and stabilityIMPG2 TABLE original.docx' differs from the paper's Table 3. Of the 23 Table 3 values it holds, 3 differ by more than 10%; SDM gives p.Asp423Glu +0.58 (Stabilizing) where Table 3 prints -0.52, MuPRO gives p.Leu249Phe -1.2666 where Table 3 prints -1.525, and mCSM gives p.Asp423Glu -0.58 against -0.653. Three more differ within 10% (SDM p.Cys1019Tyr -0.85 against -0.78, iMutant p.Arg131Cys -1.22 against -1.13, DUET p.Leu249Phe -1.777 against -1.77). It has no iMutant value for IMPG1. Its Table A names p.Leu249Phe 'p.Leu 249Tyr'. Rerun here, MuPRO gives -1.2666 for p.Leu249Phe (the document's value) and -0.887 for p.Cys1019Tyr, where both the document and Table 3 give -1.266, and I-Mutant 2.0 gives -1.22 for p.Arg131Cys (the document's value).

Table 4's p.Asp423Glu column (89,419 Da, pI 4.81, 12,457 atoms, GRAVY -0.474) is what ProtParam's definitions give for Asp423Phe on UniProt Q17R60, not for Asp423Glu (89,401.4 Da, 4.796, 12,453, -0.482); a single Asp to Glu change adds one CH2.

In Table 2 the IMPG1 SIFT scores match VEP's values for the two variants exchanged (p.Leu740Phe 0.02, p.Asp423Glu 0.09), and two variant ids are mistyped (rs15048636 for rs150486366, rs267606975 for rs267606875, which the dandiset's Word document gives).

IMPG1 p.Asp423Glu (c.1269C>A, GRCh38 6:76002940 G>T, rs758038128), which the paper calls novel, was ClinVar variation 1000102 (missense, uncertain significance, condition not provided) in every ClinVar release from 15 March 2021, including all of November 2024.

In the Figure 4 file of IMPG2 (sub-01_sample-04b) the variant labels are one row out of step with the images; the top row shows Arg131 and Cys131 and is labelled p.Cys1019Tyr, the middle row shows Cys1019 and Tyr1019 and is labelled p.Leu249Phe (read by eye).

Question for the paper's authors. Which PolyPhen-2 model (HumDiv or HumVar), which FATHMM model (the 'FATHMM coding' column) and which MutationTaster output (the 0 to 100 'score') give Table 2, on which transcript and genome build, and which CADD version; which gnomAD version and which reading of '1 in N' (the values match v4.1 joint counts as 1/(2 x allele frequency)); and which source gives the domain boundaries of Figure 1, whose IMPG1 EGF-like domain is not in UniProt and whose IMPG2 EGF-like 2 domain is not in InterPro. Also, which I-Mutant 2.0 output and sign give Table 3's iMutant column, and what made a fundus autofluorescence lesion count as hyper-autofluorescent (the right eye of M73, whose lesion holds only a speck no brighter than the background fundus).

Table 3's iMutant values for IMPG2 p.Cys1019Tyr and p.Leu249Phe (-0.14, -0.55, destabilizing) are the magnitudes the I-Mutant 2.0 server the paper names gives from sequence with the sign reversed (+0.14, +0.55, which the server prints as increased stability); the server also gives +0.19 and +0.88 for the IMPG1 variants (Table 3 -0.85 and -0.76), and its sign classifier calls p.Asp423Glu stabilizing. Table 3's MuPRO value for p.Cys1019Tyr (-1.266) is the one MuPRO gives for p.Leu249Phe.

entries.name: 001882-yuan-2025
entries.title: IMPG1 and IMPG2 variants in retinal dystrophy patients (Yuan et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Yuan, Chatterjee, Leys, Odom and Salido (2025) on dandiset 001882, which holds a table of the seven patients with IMPG1 or IMPG2 variants, a document of in silico tool outputs and the paper's four figures as image files. It checks the patients' genotypes, diagnoses and acuities, reads the phenotypes on the deposited figure panels, and retests the in silico findings (domains, pathogenicity scores, ClinVar, ProtParam values, gnomAD frequencies) with pinned outside services.
